description: A Neurosymbolic Prolog built on Python

summary.one_liner: Clausal Prolog is an ISO-conformant Prolog implemented in Python, designed to run symbolic logic and neural/Python code in one process.
summary.what_it_does: The project provides a Prolog engine in Python with three source surfaces: .clausal files (cut-free ISO-style Prolog, the default), .pl files (regular ISO Prolog including cut), and .seam files (Python-syntax modules with a ++expr escape and adapters). Modules are loaded through Python's standard import system once the clausal package is imported. The engine includes CLP(Z), CLP(B), CLP(Q), CLP(R) and dif/2 constraints, SLG tabling with well-founded negation, DCG rules, and a large standard library. Queries run on Python's asyncio event loop, and Python libraries can be reached through library(...) facades and allowlisted seam bridges. Tests can be written inline as test/1 and test/2 clauses and run with a standalone runner or pytest.
use_cases: write cut-free Prolog logic programs in Python
combine neural network predictions with symbolic rules
constraint solving over integers and puzzles like SEND+MORE
querying Prolog predicates from Python code
running tabled Prolog queries with recursion over cycles
using Python libraries such as SciPy or PyTorch from Prolog
stack: optional clausal-* packages wrapping SciPy, PyTorch, JAX, scikit-learn, spaCy, SymPy, OpenCV, PyYAML, ACL2
notable: Cut-free Clausal Prolog surface that enforces purity at load time, with dif/2 and if_/3 in place of cut and if-then-else
Three source surfaces (.clausal, .pl, .seam) importable with Python's standard import system
Queries run on Python's own asyncio event loop, with backtracking across awaits (experimental)
Python interop through library(...) facades and allowlisted python_bridges rather than arbitrary Python calls
Modules require an end_module/1 declaration by default
caveats: Requires Python 3.13 or newer and a C compiler when building from source
Files named .clausal that contain seam Python code must be renamed to .seam after the 1.0 extension change
Asyncio support and direct .pl import are marked experimental; full ISO Prolog needs the Scryer or Trealla embeddings, which are not on PyPI yet
